source_documents.title: Preparation and Photophysical Study of Rhodamine–Perylenebisimide Electron Donor–Acceptor Dyad/Triads Containing Flexible Linkers

reference_evidence_units.quote: These results propose a photo-induced electron transfer (PET) process in this compound upon photoexcitation, which is responsible for the fluorescence quenching of the dyad and triads in polar solvents.
reference_evidence_units.subject: dyad and triads
reference_evidence_units.statement: PBI fluorescence quenching is assigned to PET from the rhodamine lactam.

reference_evidence_units.quote: When the Rho moiety is in its closed form, the FRET is inhibited, and the quenching of the fluorescence is mainly due to PET.
reference_evidence_units.subject: closed-ring Rho conjugates
reference_evidence_units.statement: With the lactam closed, energy transfer is off and PET quenches.

reference_evidence_units.quote: demonstrate that the PET is thermodynamically allowed for all dyads and triads [39–41].
reference_evidence_units.subject: all three
reference_evidence_units.statement: ΔGCS is negative (about -0.4 to -1.0 eV) in all solvents studied.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Nevertheless, fluorescence measurements reveal that the emission of the PBI unit is strongly quenched, even in non-polar solvents such as toluene.
reference_evidence_units.subject: all three
reference_evidence_units.statement: ΦF in toluene 0.2% (Et triad), 1.7% (HEX triad), 5.9% (HEX dyad) vs 95.2% for PBI-Br (Table 1).

reference_evidence_units.quote: Nanosecond transient absorption measurements confirm the formation of the PBI triplet excited state (lifetime is up to 126 µs).
reference_evidence_units.subject: dyad and triads

reference_evidence_units.quote: The production of the trace triplet state is probably due to the CR.
reference_evidence_units.subject: dyad and triads
reference_evidence_units.statement: The triplet comes from charge recombination (CR-induced ISC).

reference_evidence_units.quote: However, the mutual orientation of the PBI and the Rho units in the dyad and triads is not fixed; therefore, the CR-induced ISC is non-efficient (for instance, the situation is not optimized for the SOCT-ISC mechanism).
reference_evidence_units.subject: dyad and triads

reference_evidence_units.quote: While a Förster resonance energy transfer (FRET) probably occurs between PBI and the open-ring rhodamine, a photo-induced electron transfer is proposed to be responsible for the quenching of the fluorescence of the PBI moiety.
reference_evidence_units.subject: dyad and triads
reference_evidence_units.statement: FRET needs the ring-opened rhodamine; PET explains the quenching.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Neither FRET nor charge separation/charge recombination processes were observed with fs-TA spectra, despite the quenching of the fluorescence, which may be due to the ultrafast electron transfer or the energy transfer processes.
reference_evidence_units.subject: dyad and triads
reference_evidence_units.statement: No CS state is resolved in fs-TA.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: The PET assignment is not confirmed by transient radical-ion bands.

reference_mechanisms.label: PET_ET
reference_mechanisms.rationale: PBI emission is strongly quenched (Table 1) and Rehm-Weller ΔGCS is negative; the paper assigns the quenching to PET from the closed rhodamine lactam. fs-TA does not resolve the CS state (E09). ΦF 1.7% with the hexylene linker.

reference_mechanisms.label: TRIPLET_ISC_RTP_TADF
reference_mechanisms.rationale: A long-lived PBI triplet (ns-TA) and low singlet-oxygen yields, attributed to inefficient charge-recombination ISC.

out_of_pool: FRET to the ring-opened rhodamine (another form of the donor) (E08)

contrast_group.varied_factor: alkyl linker between the rhodamine lactams and PBI (ethylene vs hexylene)
contrast_group.paper_difference: The short ethylene linker quenches PBI emission more strongly (ΦF 0.2% vs 1.7% in toluene) and gives more singlet oxygen (Φ∆ 2.9% vs 2.1%).
